title: sdui-parser (renderer/preview copy): a  attribute still overwrites the html-tier discriminator — objectstack now refuses it at parse
body:
Surfaced while implementing objectstack#13957 (objectstack PR #14274), which lands the maintainer's 2026-09-01 ruling on the objectstack side. Filed rather than folded in: that PR is `packages/sdui-parser` in objectstack, and this half is this repo's copy.

## What objectstack just changed

On a `kind:'html'` page the tag name **is** the node's `type`, so an authored `type=` attribute is a name collision with the envelope's discriminator. objectstack's copy of the parser now **refuses it at parse time** with one `forbidden-attr` error naming both the tag and the attribute, and builds the node as `{ ...props, type: tag }` instead of `{ type: tag, ...props }`.

Before that, two outcomes: when the authored value named another **registered** type (a `flex` element carrying `type="grid"`), the tree carried the author's value as its discriminator, the manifest resolved it, every check passed, and a different component rendered with **zero diagnostics**; when it named nothing registered, `unknown-component` blamed the *value* and read as a missing plugin.

## This repo's copy still does the old thing

`packages/sdui-parser/src/parse.ts` here builds the node as:

```ts
const node: SchemaElement = markHtmlTierNode({ type: tag, ...props });
```

`props` spread after `type: tag`, and no refusal in `parseAttr` — so the renderer-side and live-preview copy still accepts the attribute and still lets it win the discriminator slot.

## Why this is filed and not urgent-by-default

The direction of the divergence is the safe one: objectstack runs the **save gate** and is now the stricter of the two, so a refused page never reaches a renderer that would misread it. That is the opposite of the save-clean-renders-inert failure the lockstep exists to prevent (objectstack#12719). ⚠️ But the two copies now differ in accepted grammar, and the live **edit preview** in the console runs this copy — an author gets no diagnostic while typing and a refusal on save.

Note the refusal deliberately reuses the existing `forbidden-attr` code rather than minting a new one, precisely so `check:sdui-lockstep` stays green in both directions; a port here needs no new code either.

## What a port would be

1. Refuse a `type` attribute in `parseAttr` with the existing `forbidden-attr` code, one diagnostic naming both the tag and the attribute.
2. Reverse the spread: `markHtmlTierNode({ ...props, type: tag })` — defense in depth, correct only *because* of (1); reversing it alone trades a silent overwrite for a silent discard.
3. ⛔ Do **not** carry the react tier's `specType` rescue (objectui#2880) into the html tier — the ruling declined it by name; that rescue stays where it lives.
4. After it lands, objectstack re-records its side with `pnpm gen:sdui-lockstep` when the `.objectui-sha` pin moves.

The ruled decision and its rationale are recorded as an append-only amendment on objectstack's ADR-0080.
